experiment_description: Central concept tested: a modified Hanbury Brown–Twiss interferometer is used to determine whether classical pseudothermal light can exhibit one-zero photon-number-projection antibunching when ordinary single-photon detectors are treated as photon-number-resolving detectors by binning their time-tagged outputs. A single-mode continuous-wave laser at 780 nm center wavelength with 200 kHz frequency bandwidth is incident on a rotating ground glass to generate pseudothermal light; the laser intensity is adjusted with a variable light-intensity attenuator, and the laser spot size on the rotating ground glass is controlled by the lens-to-ground-glass distance. The scattered light is split by a 1:1 non-polarizing beam splitter. Two single-mode-fiber couplers with 4.0 µm core-diameter fibers define the two detection modes and send light to two single-photon detectors D1 and D2. The fiber couplers are placed at symmetric output positions of the beamsplitter for the temporal measurement, with no spatial scan. Photon arrival times from D1 and D2 are recorded on a common clock using a HydraHarp 400 photon detection time-series module, and the offline analysis bins the events into time bins of T = 1 µs. The D1 and D2 single-photon count rates used for this temporal data set are 734.57 kHz and 583.82 kHz, corresponding to 0.73 and 0.58 detected photons per bin and an averaged photon number per detector of \bar n = 0.66. For each integer m = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, the measured quantity is g_m0^(2)(τ), the normalized correlation between the event “D1 detects m photons in a bin” and “D2 detects zero photons in a bin,” normalized by the corresponding marginal probabilities; τ is the relative delay between detector time bins. The temporal correlation is evaluated over the plotted delay window from −30 µs to +30 µs, and the zero-delay value is obtained from the peak or dip at τ = 0 relative to the long-delay background. The spatial scope is the single pair of symmetric fiber-coupled detection modes at the beamsplitter outputs; the lateral detection-mode aperture is set by the 4.0 µm single-mode fiber cores, and no independent repeated sample count or scan step size is reported.

temporal_pseudothermal_g00_zero_delay.description: The zero-delay normalized temporal correlation for D1 detecting zero photons and D2 detecting zero photons, obtained from the τ = 0 feature relative to the long-delay background.

temporal_pseudothermal_g10_zero_delay.description: The zero-delay normalized temporal correlation for D1 detecting one photon and D2 detecting zero photons, obtained from the τ = 0 feature relative to the long-delay background.

temporal_pseudothermal_g20_zero_delay.description: The zero-delay normalized temporal correlation for D1 detecting two photons and D2 detecting zero photons, obtained from the τ = 0 feature relative to the long-delay background.

temporal_pseudothermal_g30_zero_delay.description: The zero-delay normalized temporal correlation for D1 detecting three photons and D2 detecting zero photons, obtained from the τ = 0 feature relative to the long-delay background.

temporal_pseudothermal_g40_zero_delay.description: The zero-delay normalized temporal correlation for D1 detecting four photons and D2 detecting zero photons, obtained from the τ = 0 feature relative to the long-delay background.

experiment_description: Central concept tested: the modified HBT photon-number-projection measurement is compared for pseudothermal light and coherent laser light to determine whether the one-zero projection correlation depends jointly on thermal photon statistics and photon-number binning. The optical layout is the same two-output beamsplitter geometry with two single-mode-fiber-coupled single-photon detectors and HydraHarp 400 time-tag recording. For the pseudothermal-light data, a 780 nm single-mode continuous-wave laser with 200 kHz bandwidth is scattered from a rotating ground glass before a 1:1 non-polarizing beamsplitter; for the laser-light control, the rotating ground glass is removed so that the 780 nm single-mode continuous-wave laser directly enters the interferometer. The variable attenuator sweeps the input intensity, and for every setting the photon records are binned into T = 1 µs time bins. The independent variable \bar n is the average number of detected photons per detector per bin, obtained by averaging the binned counts from D1 and D2. The plotted sweep covers approximately \bar n = 0 to 0.66. The measured quantities are zero-delay normalized photon-number-projection correlations g_m0^(2)(0), where m = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 for pseudothermal light and m = 1 for the laser-light control; g_m0^(2)(0) is defined as the joint probability for m detections in D1 and zero detections in D2 at zero relative delay divided by the product of the corresponding marginal probabilities. The spatial detection scope is the same fixed pair of fiber-coupled beamsplitter output modes as in the temporal experiment, with 4.0 µm fiber-core modal apertures and no spatial scan; the plotted points correspond to a single intensity sweep, and no independent repeated sample count or scan step size is reported.

laser_g10_zero_delay_over_nbar_sweep.description: The empirical dependence of the zero-delay one-zero normalized correlation for the coherent-laser control over the reported average-photon-number sweep. Here g_{10,L}^{(2)}(0; \bar n) denotes the laser-light value as a function of the average detected photon number per detector per 1 µs bin.

pseudothermal_g00_zero_delay_at_nbar_0p6.description: The zero-delay normalized correlation for zero detections in D1 and zero detections in D2 at the high end of the reported pseudothermal-light intensity sweep.

pseudothermal_g40_zero_delay_at_nbar_0p6.description: The zero-delay normalized correlation for four detections in D1 and zero detections in D2 at the high end of the reported pseudothermal-light intensity sweep.

experiment_description: Central concept tested: the modified HBT photon-number-projection scheme is configured to detect spatial one-zero projection correlations of classical pseudothermal light and to determine whether changing the bin-defined average photon number can switch the spatial g_10^(2) feature between suppression and enhancement. A 780 nm single-mode continuous-wave laser with 200 kHz bandwidth illuminates a rotating ground glass to produce pseudothermal light, which is split by a 1:1 non-polarizing beamsplitter. The two output modes are coupled into 4.0 µm core-diameter single-mode fibers and detected by two single-photon detectors whose time tags are recorded by a HydraHarp 400. D2 is held fixed at a reference output position, while D1 is mounted on motorized x-y translation stages and scanned horizontally through the corresponding output beam; the plotted horizontal displacement is Δx from −1.0 mm to +1.0 mm, with Δx = 0 corresponding to the symmetric-position alignment of the two detection modes. The reported scan is a single horizontal line scan through the coupled detection mode; the fiber core sets the lateral modal aperture, while the scan step size, beam waist at the coupler, and number of repeated scans are not specified. For each Δx, g_m0^(2)(Δx) is computed by dividing the local peak or dip value by the far-displacement background for m = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Two binned-photon regimes are measured using the same optical geometry: a T = 1 µs bin giving \bar n = 0.66 average detected photons per detector, and a T = 3 µs bin giving \bar n = 1.98 average detected photons per detector; \bar n is calculated by averaging D1 and D2 detected photon numbers.
